modes.claim_ceiling: live session evidence to that verifier

modes.witness: delegated notary participates and signs Session Header
modes.claim_ceiling: portable only under explicit notary trust profile

modes.witness: verifier proxies encrypted traffic and verifies TLS proof
attestation node validates TLS provenance, extracts a field and signs a salted value commitment; client proves commitment/signature/policy in a transparent STARK
modes.portability: portable proof under explicit attestation-node, STARK and aggregator profiles
modes.claim_ceiling: the proof is linked to the attestor-signed extracted value; source extraction correctness inherits the attestation-node trust assumption

modes.witness: prover and verifier jointly participate in a three-party TLS handshake with the web server
modes.claim_ceiling: the verifier checks exact TLS data provenance and selective opening under DECO's exact construction; context integrity and collusion assumptions remain explicit

modes.witness: paper-specific three-party TLS/MPC protocol for restricted TLS 1.3 websites
modes.claim_ceiling: only the exact DIDO+ implementation/profile; no qualification inheritance to DECO or TLSNotary

modes.witness: zkPass documented hybrid of proxy mode and MPC mode with VOLE-based ZK
modes.claim_ceiling: mode, witness/network assumptions and exact release remain explicit

modes.witness: split TEE services with hardware attestation and MPC/TLS proof path
modes.claim_ceiling: trust is conditional on the exact TEE vendor chain, image measurement, hardware/configuration and split-service threat model

nonclaims: TLSNotary does not establish provider business truth.
An authenticated response does not establish account ownership or legal entitlement.
A notary signature does not remove trust in the delegated in-session witness.
Proxy mode is not security-equivalent to MPC-TLS.
Selective disclosure does not establish anonymity.
A request-bound balance proof is not a TLS transcript commitment opening.
TLS 1.3 support must be established from the exact release, not roadmap language.
Scribe-style salted commitment nullifiers do not guarantee account-level or person-level uniqueness across fresh salts.
Falcon-signed aggregator roots authenticate the root signer but do not by themselves prove append-only state transition correctness.
A circuit-friendly attestation signature is not automatically a standard or post-quantum signature.
TLS 1.3 support in one research protocol does not qualify TLS 1.3 support in another TLS-provenance implementation.
A valid TEE quote does not establish source authenticity unless exact measured code, TCB and dataflow roles are qualified.
A scoped nullifier does not establish person-level uniqueness unless a domain-authorized subject binding connects the relevant accounts/credentials.

cases.scenario: Relying verifier participates online in MPC-TLS and verifies the exact server identity, transcript opening and application predicate.
cases.invariant: Only the participating verifier receives the designated-verifier claim.

cases.scenario: Delegated notary signs a Session Header; later verifier validates the notary signature, transcript opening, TLS-specific server data and server identity.
cases.invariant: Portability inherits the declared notary trust root.

cases.scenario: Proxy verifier observes encrypted traffic and verifies the exact admitted TLS 1.2 session proof under an explicit proxy profile.
cases.invariant: Proxy evidence never upgrades to MPC-TLS profile.

cases.scenario: An offline relying party treats a notary-signed presentation as trustless proof with no notary dependency.
cases.invariant: Attestation verifier inherits trust in the delegated in-session witness.

cases.scenario: A third party who did not participate treats a direct-verifier transcript as portable public proof.
cases.invariant: Direct verifier evidence is designated-verifier.

cases.scenario: Proxy result is admitted where the policy requires MPC-TLS's server-identity privacy or direct prover-to-server network path.
cases.invariant: Proxy mode has a distinct trust model and server-identity disclosure.

cases.scenario: A Session Header is validly signed by a key outside the expected notary trust-root/key-epoch profile.
cases.invariant: Signature validity under an unexpected key is not notary qualification.

cases.scenario: The notary signature verifies but the supplied plaintext opening does not match the committed root.
cases.invariant: Notary signature and commitment opening are independently checked.

cases.scenario: The transcript commitment matches, but the prover substitutes a private balance unrelated to the selected committed field.
cases.invariant: The proof must link one witness to the exact committed field and predicate.

cases.scenario: A correct opening is checked with a different HTTP-object leaf index or range selector.
cases.invariant: The exact selector and opening path are part of the statement.

cases.scenario: The exact response is parsed with a substituted parser version, duplicate-key policy or JSON Pointer.
cases.invariant: Parser identity and selection semantics are committed into the proof.

cases.scenario: Currency, decimal scale, sign, rounding or inclusive/exclusive comparison changes while the numeric threshold remains the same.
cases.invariant: Claim schema and exact predicate semantics are separately bound.

cases.scenario: Valid server session is presented for the wrong origin, SNI, method, path, query, deployment or API product.
cases.invariant: Exact source request/profile is part of the claim.

cases.scenario: Wrong TLS version or cipher suite is accepted despite the frozen protocol profile.
cases.invariant: TLS version and cipher profile are explicit.

cases.scenario: A TLS 1.3-only provider is admitted while the pinned TLSNotary release only qualifies TLS 1.2.
cases.invariant: Roadmap intent is not release capability.

cases.scenario: A valid authenticated response is semantically false or misleading.
cases.invariant: Transport authenticity does not establish business truth.

cases.scenario: A successful provider login is treated as proof that the prover legally owns every returned account.
cases.invariant: Authentication is not account ownership or beneficial entitlement.

cases.scenario: The same commitment root, server metadata or account identifier correlates separate presentations across audiences.
cases.invariant: Selective disclosure is not anonymity; linkability is measured.

cases.scenario: Repeated threshold predicates allow an adaptive verifier to infer a low-entropy private balance.
cases.invariant: Predicate sequences are a privacy channel.

cases.scenario: A presentation reveals cookies, authorization headers, bearer tokens, account IDs or unrelated response fields.
cases.invariant: Only explicitly permitted fields may leave the prover.

cases.scenario: A request challenge, audience, purpose or policy is replayed/substituted across sessions.
cases.invariant: Exact request binding and consume-once challenge ownership are required.

cases.scenario: A previously valid response remains cryptographically authentic but is outside the required freshness interval or has been superseded.
cases.invariant: Cryptographic provenance is not currentness; LISE requalifies dependencies.

cases.scenario: A host supplies source_valid=true, a parser output or a request digest without the corresponding authenticated root/opening evidence.
cases.invariant: Host booleans and reference digests are not source proof.

cases.scenario: A receipt valid for a different Symthaea guest ImageID is offered to the request-bound predicate verifier.
cases.invariant: The expected exact guest ImageID is verifier-owned.

cases.scenario: Attestation node witnesses the exact TLS session, applies a frozen extraction rule, signs a commitment, and the STARK proves the policy over the same committed value.
cases.invariant: This is valid only under the declared attestation-node trust assumption and exact extraction profile.

cases.scenario: The same Web2 account obtains a second attestation using a fresh salt, producing a different commitment and different spend tag, then claims a second one-time entitlement.
cases.invariant: A salted commitment-derived spend tag prevents same-tag replay, not necessarily repeat claims by the same account. Uniqueness subject and privacy-preserving subject binding must be explicit.

cases.scenario: The attestation node signs a value commitment without executing or verifying a genuine TLS provenance session.
cases.invariant: Base Scribe-style security assumes the attestation node behaves correctly; a signature cannot prove the witness actually ran the protocol.

cases.scenario: A client substitutes application ID, server ID, extraction rule, data or salt after receiving an attestation signature.
cases.invariant: Every authority/privacy-relevant field must be covered by one unambiguous, domain-separated commitment preimage and signature.

cases.scenario: An in-circuit attestation signature implementation is treated as EUF-CMA secure without exact construction review, multi-message analysis, key-lifecycle rules or independent cryptanalysis.
cases.invariant: Circuit-friendly does not mean standard, secure or post-quantum; theorem assumptions must match the exact deployed construction.

cases.scenario: Aggregator publishes a Falcon-signed new root that omits a previously accepted spend tag or equivocates between two roots.
cases.invariant: A signature authenticates the root signer; it does not prove append-only correctness, inclusion of accepted submissions or consistency with the prior root.

cases.scenario: Deployment labels the whole credential pipeline post-quantum because the aggregator root is Falcon-signed, while TLS and attestation signatures use classical assumptions.
cases.invariant: Post-quantum status is layer-specific; PQ root authorization does not promote the attestation, TLS, commitment or complete protocol.

cases.scenario: A response has ambiguous JSON/canonicalization or duplicate-key interpretation and the attestation node and prover use different extraction semantics.
cases.invariant: The exact parser/canonicalization and extraction-rule version must be frozen and bound into the signed commitment.

cases.scenario: A ZK proof reveals no private witness, but request timing, response size, attestation metadata or repeated queries correlate the same subject across sessions.
cases.invariant: Proof zero-knowledge does not hide network metadata, timing, sizes or linkability across repeated predicates.

cases.scenario: An application-scoped spend tag is expected to guarantee legal-person uniqueness even though no domain-qualified subject binding connects accounts to that person.
cases.invariant: Account, legal person, credential, entitlement and application are distinct uniqueness subjects. A nullifier cannot prove real-world uniqueness by itself.

cases.scenario: The prover reveals a selected substring that appears in multiple places or can be interpreted differently, without proving the required surrounding context and exact response position.
cases.invariant: Selective opening must preserve context integrity; substring presence alone does not establish the intended semantic field.

cases.scenario: An implementation using DECO or TLSNotary claims TLS 1.3 coverage solely because a separate DIDO+ paper demonstrates a TLS 1.3 research protocol.
cases.invariant: TLS-version support is implementation- and profile-specific; no protocol inherits another paper's negotiated-version capability.

cases.scenario: A proxy-mode zkPass presentation is admitted under a profile that requires the MPC-mode or another direct-verifier network-path assumption.
cases.invariant: Proxy and MPC are distinct protocol profiles; hybrid fallback does not permit cross-mode qualification inheritance.

cases.scenario: The deployment selects MPC mode without enforcing the declared bandwidth, response-size and resource limits for the exact protocol release.
cases.invariant: Protocol mode and workload bounds are part of qualification; throughput figures from proxy mode do not establish MPC feasibility.

cases.scenario: A hardware quote verifies cryptographically but its TEE image measurement, firmware chain, cloud configuration or security version does not match the admitted profile.
cases.invariant: A valid quote is not enough; exact measurement, vendor root, TCB version and policy must match.

cases.scenario: The split TEE architecture is reduced to a generic tee_attested=true flag, losing which service held TLS keys, which service saw request/response data, and which code measurement each quote binds.
cases.invariant: TEE roles, data visibility, measurements and trust domains must remain separately represented and qualified.

cases.scenario: The same provider account and same entitlement are re-attested with a different random salt and fresh commitment; the second proof attempts to claim the same scoped benefit.
cases.invariant: The salt must not define uniqueness identity; a domain-qualified stable hidden subject binding is required for same-account/entitlement uniqueness.

cases.scenario: The same qualified issuer-bound subject obtains a fresh randomized presentation/credential for the same application entitlement scope; the scoped nullifier remains the same and the second consume is blocked.
cases.invariant: Presentation randomness and credential re-issuance must not reset same-scope uniqueness when subject continuity is established.

cases.scenario: Two provider accounts are asserted to belong to the same natural/legal person, but no qualified common subject-binding credential or authority exists.
cases.invariant: Account-level uniqueness is not person-level uniqueness; do not infer identity from names, email, device or graph correlation.

cases.scenario: Issuer key rotation, account recovery, account merge or credential replacement changes the apparent subject secret without a qualified continuity/migration proof.
cases.invariant: Recovery and rotation cannot silently mint a new uniqueness identity; historical consumption remains append-only.

cases.scenario: A policy digest changes while the application entitlement is still the same, and the new proof derives a new nullifier as if the subject had never claimed.
cases.invariant: A policy version change does not automatically reset the uniqueness scope; the domain owner must explicitly define a new entitlement epoch.

cases.scenario: The same subject's scoped nullifiers for two unrelated applications are publicly linkable through a stable global subject pseudonym.
cases.invariant: Uniqueness is deliberately linkable only within the declared scope; no global stable subject handle is published.

cases.scenario: A Beta.1 transcript commitment is reordered, duplicated or substituted after the commitment-order-preservation boundary.
cases.invariant: The exact transcript commitment order is part of the authenticated statement; reordering cannot preserve acceptance.

cases.scenario: Prover-supplied transcript commitment ranges are reversed, overlapping, duplicated, empty, overflowed or outside configured transcript bounds.
cases.invariant: Range validation must be enforced by the exact pinned implementation; attacker-controlled ranges cannot trigger unbounded work or ambiguous openings.

cases.scenario: Verifier and prover compute different GHASH byte ordering or a transcript is verified against a wrong byte-order known-answer vector.
cases.invariant: Exact GHASH byte order and TLS transcript authenticity must match the pinned beta.1 implementation.

cases.scenario: The application intentionally accepts the entire response as non-sensitive; full-reveal path transfers the response write key, verifier decrypts the whole direction, and the TLS key-derivation ZK proof still verifies.
cases.invariant: Full reveal skips response ciphertext-to-plaintext ZK work but does not skip the key-derivation proof; this is not selective disclosure.

cases.scenario: A response contains one sensitive byte or field but is benchmarked/admitted as full reveal, disclosing the entire response or incorrectly claiming selective privacy.
cases.invariant: One private byte/field prevents full-reveal treatment for that direction; all-or-nothing direction semantics must be explicit.

cases.scenario: Peer close, EOF, partial proxy write, cancellation or stream-limit mismatch causes a session to hang, busy-loop or silently drop transcript bytes.
cases.invariant: A session must either complete deterministically or fail with an observable transport error; configured mux limits must match both peers.

privacy_profiles.disclosure: entire selected traffic direction is revealed to verifier
privacy_profiles.zk_cost: TLS key-derivation proof remains; direction plaintext proof skipped
privacy_profiles.admission: only when entire direction is approved for disclosure

privacy_profiles.disclosure: only selected ranges/HTTP objects revealed; unrelated fields redacted
privacy_profiles.zk_cost: commitment/opening and relevant plaintext proof required

privacy_profiles.disclosure: one or more sensitive bytes remain hidden within direction
privacy_profiles.zk_cost: full direction ZK path applies; full-reveal fast path unavailable
privacy_profiles.admission: must not be benchmarked as full reveal
